answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions conditional on a rotating stake: each identity locks tokens, and a randomly selected nebula of peers challenges its work before release. A challenge backed by evidence slashes the stake and records the failed key, while honest completion returns it after a delay. Splitting one account into many does not multiply influence without multiplying locked capital, so a sybil attacker must tie up funds across identities and risks losing them. Ferrous hardware or a crystal avatar cannot substitute for that economic cost.
